description: Original beginner-friendly study questions. Independent practice, not official exam items. Covers every domain; not a complete objective bank or a weighted exam simulation.

questions.prompt: An online store has large traffic spikes during sales. Which cloud benefit lets it add capacity during a sale and remove it afterward?

choices.explanation: Elasticity adjusts capacity as demand rises and falls, helping avoid idle resources after the sale.
Provisioning for the largest possible peak leaves paid capacity idle between sales.
A fixed-size server cannot automatically grow with demand and shrink afterward.
Monitoring helps detect demand; disabling it does not provide flexible capacity.

questions.prompt: A team wants its application to keep running if one data center fails. Which design is most appropriate?

choices.text: Place all servers on one physical host
choices.explanation: One physical host creates a single point of failure.
Availability Zones provide isolated locations within a Region. A properly designed multi-AZ application can tolerate a zone failure.

choices.text: Make a larger server in one Availability Zone
choices.explanation: A larger server increases capacity but does not protect against loss of its Availability Zone.

choices.text: Keep only one copy of the application data
choices.explanation: One copy increases the risk of losing access to data; redundancy is needed.

questions.prompt: A company moves its existing virtual machines to Amazon EC2 with minimal application changes. Which migration strategy is this?

choices.explanation: Retiring removes an application that is no longer needed rather than moving it.
Refactoring changes the application architecture to use cloud capabilities more fully.
Rehosting, often called lift and shift, moves an application with minimal changes.
Retaining keeps the application in its existing environment for now.

questions.prompt: Which TWO changes commonly occur when moving from owned servers to pay-as-you-go cloud resources?

choices.text: Replace some upfront hardware spending with usage-based spending
choices.explanation: Cloud usage can shift capital expenditure toward operating expenditure.
Cloud resources, support, networking, and administration can still incur expenses.

choices.text: Stop paying for unused compute after terminating eligible resources
choices.explanation: Terminating on-demand compute stops its compute usage charge; separately retained storage or other resources can still cost money.

choices.text: Guarantee every workload will cost less
choices.explanation: Savings depend on architecture, utilization, pricing choices, and operational discipline.

questions.prompt: Which action follows the reliability principle of testing recovery procedures?

choices.text: Assume a successful backup guarantees recovery
choices.explanation: A backup can be unusable or incomplete; restoration needs verification.

choices.text: Remove all backup copies to reduce complexity
choices.explanation: Removing backups removes a recovery option and increases risk.

choices.text: Wait until a production outage to try restoring
choices.explanation: An outage is a poor time to discover that recovery steps do not work.

choices.text: Regularly restore a backup in a safe test environment
choices.explanation: Restore exercises validate both the backup and the documented recovery process before an outage.

questions.prompt: A company runs a Linux server on Amazon EC2. Under shared responsibility, which task belongs to the customer?

choices.explanation: For EC2, customers manage their guest operating systems, applications, and configurations.

choices.text: Replace failed disks in the AWS data center
choices.explanation: AWS maintains the underlying physical infrastructure.

choices.text: Control physical entry to the AWS data center
choices.explanation: AWS is responsible for physical data center security.
AWS manages the host infrastructure that supports EC2.

questions.prompt: An application on EC2 needs permission to read one S3 bucket. What is the best approach?

choices.text: Embed the root account password in the application
choices.explanation: Root credentials are highly privileged and must not be embedded in code.
Public access exposes data and does not follow least privilege.

choices.text: Attach an IAM role with limited S3 permissions to the instance
choices.explanation: An instance role supplies temporary credentials and can restrict access to the required bucket.

choices.text: Email a permanent administrator access key to every developer
choices.explanation: Long-lived administrator keys create unnecessary privilege and exposure.

questions.prompt: Which TWO practices help protect an AWS account?

choices.text: Enable multi-factor authentication for the root user
choices.explanation: MFA adds a verification factor beyond a password for sensitive root access.

choices.text: Use the root user for daily administration
choices.explanation: Root should be reserved for tasks that require it, not routine work.

choices.text: Share one administrator identity with the whole team
choices.explanation: Shared identities reduce accountability and make access removal difficult.

choices.text: Grant only the permissions each role needs
choices.explanation: Least privilege limits damage from mistakes or compromised credentials.

questions.prompt: An auditor asks who changed a security group rule through an AWS API. Which service records this account activity?

choices.explanation: Route 53 provides DNS and routing features, not a general API activity audit trail.
CloudTrail records AWS account API activity, including identity and request details for supported events.
Glacier storage classes support archival storage, not API event auditing by themselves.
Pricing Calculator estimates costs and does not record configuration changes.

questions.prompt: A compliance team needs AWS compliance reports and certain agreements. Which service should it use?

choices.explanation: Auto Scaling changes compute capacity; it is not the compliance report portal.
CloudFormation provisions resources from templates rather than providing AWS compliance reports.
Artifact provides on-demand access to AWS security and compliance reports and select agreements.
CloudFront delivers cached content near users; it does not provide compliance report access.

questions.prompt: A team stores private objects in S3. Which responsibility remains with the customer?

choices.explanation: AWS operates and maintains the physical storage infrastructure.

choices.text: Controlling access to the AWS building
choices.explanation: Physical facility security is an AWS responsibility.

choices.text: Maintaining the S3 service operating system
choices.explanation: AWS manages the underlying software infrastructure for the managed S3 service.

choices.text: Configuring appropriate access permissions for the objects
choices.explanation: Customers control their data and must configure access policies to meet their requirements.

questions.prompt: A small website needs virtual servers with control of the operating system. Which AWS service fits?

choices.explanation: Athena runs queries on data, commonly in S3, rather than hosting general-purpose virtual servers.
EC2 supplies virtual compute instances on which customers can manage the operating system.
Budgets tracks costs and usage against thresholds; it is not a compute host.
Route 53 is a DNS service and does not run a guest operating system for the website.

questions.prompt: An application needs durable object storage for uploaded photos. Which service is the best fit?

choices.explanation: S3 stores objects such as photos and supports durable storage at scale.
EBS is block storage for EC2, not a native object storage service.
Route 53 resolves DNS names; it is not a file or object store.
IAM manages access permissions rather than storing application photos.

questions.prompt: A developer needs a managed relational database compatible with MySQL. Which service is appropriate?

choices.explanation: CloudFront is a content delivery network, not a relational database.
DynamoDB is a NoSQL database rather than a MySQL-compatible relational database.
RDS manages relational database engines including MySQL, reducing infrastructure administration.
SQS queues messages between components; it is not a relational database.

questions.prompt: A function should run when a file arrives, without the team provisioning servers. Which service fits?

choices.explanation: Direct Connect provides dedicated network connectivity; it does not execute application functions.
EBS provides block volumes and does not execute event-driven code.
Organizations governs multiple accounts rather than running functions.
Lambda runs code in response to supported events without customers provisioning or managing servers.

questions.prompt: Which TWO services have the described networking roles?

choices.text: Amazon VPC provides a logically isolated network for AWS resources
choices.explanation: VPC lets customers define network ranges, subnets, routes, and related controls.

choices.text: AWS IAM caches website images at edge locations
choices.explanation: IAM manages identities and permissions; CloudFront provides edge content delivery.
Route 53 can host DNS records and route clients to application endpoints.

choices.text: Amazon RDS supplies a dedicated physical network link from an office
choices.explanation: RDS is a database service; Direct Connect provides dedicated network connectivity.

questions.prompt: How do an AWS Region and an Availability Zone relate?

choices.text: An Availability Zone always spans multiple Regions
choices.explanation: An Availability Zone is contained within a single Region.

choices.text: A Region contains multiple isolated Availability Zones
choices.explanation: A Region is a geographic area containing multiple isolated Availability Zones.

choices.text: A Region is a single customer virtual network
choices.explanation: A VPC is a logical network; a Region is a geographic infrastructure area.

choices.text: They are two names for exactly the same thing
choices.explanation: Regions and Availability Zones are different infrastructure concepts.

questions.prompt: A team wants an alert when monthly AWS spending approaches a chosen amount. Which service should it configure?

choices.explanation: CloudTrail records account activity rather than defining spending thresholds.
Route 53 manages DNS, not monthly budget alerts.
Budgets supports cost or usage budgets and notifications when defined thresholds are reached or forecast.
Auto Scaling adjusts capacity; it does not provide a monthly spending-budget alert by itself.

questions.prompt: Which TWO tools suit these cost-management tasks?

choices.text: AWS Pricing Calculator to estimate a planned architecture
choices.explanation: Pricing Calculator estimates charges from proposed service configurations before deployment.

choices.text: AWS Artifact to stop all charges at a dollar threshold
choices.explanation: Artifact supplies compliance resources and does not enforce a spending cap.

choices.text: AWS IAM to graph last month’s service spending
choices.explanation: IAM controls access; Cost Explorer is designed for spend analysis.

choices.text: AWS Cost Explorer to analyze historical costs
choices.explanation: Cost Explorer helps visualize and analyze cost and usage data over time.

questions.prompt: A batch job can tolerate interruptions and restart later. Which EC2 pricing option can reduce compute cost by using spare capacity?

choices.text: Dedicated Hosts solely for this discount
choices.explanation: Dedicated Hosts offer physical server allocation and licensing options, not the spare-capacity interruption model.
Spot uses spare EC2 capacity at discounted rates, but AWS can interrupt the instances.

choices.text: On-Demand Instances with guaranteed zero cost
choices.explanation: On-Demand offers usage-based pricing, not guaranteed free compute.
S3 storage classes price stored objects, not EC2 compute capacity.
